business_problem: St James's Hospital needed to modernize aging laboratory infrastructure because legacy on-premises systems slowed genomic diagnostics, limited storage for sequencing data, complicated ISO 15189 compliance and reduced the speed and resilience required for cancer care and research.
solution_summary: St James's Hospital worked with EY and Microsoft to replace legacy laboratory infrastructure with a bespoke cloud platform for genomic diagnostics. The team migrated on-premises data infrastructure to Azure so high volumes of genome-sequencing data could be stored, protected and accessed more efficiently across laboratory teams. Multiple laboratory systems, analyzers and equipment were connected into the new environment, while cloud-based genome sequencing tools gave scientists continuous access to data and results. Microsoft Fabric added parallel data-analysis pipelines and automated overnight processes, and machine learning was used to derive critical insights from genomic data for diagnosis and treatment planning. The architecture improved backup resilience, strengthened security controls and supported ISO 15189 requirements while making cancer-screening and molecular-testing workflows faster, more scalable and easier to operate.

data_flow: Patient specimens are sequenced and the resulting genomic data is stored in Azure, where multiple laboratory systems feed the cloud environment. Microsoft Fabric runs parallel analysis pipelines and automated overnight processes, machine learning derives clinically relevant insights, and laboratory scientists use the cloud-based sequencing tools to retrieve results and report findings across the service.
business_outcome: St James's Hospital improved resilience, compliance and diagnostic speed for cancer care by giving laboratory teams faster genomic analysis, continuous access to cloud tools and stronger security for sensitive patient data, while also reducing turnaround times for results and reporting.
